title: Understanding Residuals
text: The residual vector e is calculated as the difference between the observed values Y and the predicted values \hat{Y}.

title: Dimensions of Vectors
text: The residual vector e has the same number of elements as the number of observations in the dataset. The parameter vector \hat{\theta} has the same number of elements as the number of predictors plus one (for the intercept).

title: Comparing Dimensions
text: If there are $$n$$ observations and $$p$$ predictors, what is the dimension of the residual vector e?

title: Parameter Vector Dimension
text: If there are $$p$$ predictors, what is the dimension of the parameter vector \hat{\theta}?

title: Conclusion
text: The residual vector e and the parameter vector \hat{\theta} do not have the same dimension. The residual vector has a dimension equal to the number of observations, while the parameter vector has a dimension equal to the number of predictors plus one.
